answers.description: A toy 3D renderer implemented in Go, progressing from a CPU software renderer to GPU-accelerated real-time rendering via WebGPU.
answers.problem: Understanding 3D graphics from first principles — implementing the full pipeline (CPU → GPU) rather than using a black-box engine.
answers.target_users: The author — a developer learning 3D graphics and GPU programming through hands-on implementation.
answers.key_goals: Learn the full 3D pipeline from scratch (math → rasterization → GPU shaders); produce working, well-tested code at each phase; build toward real-time GPU rendering via WebGPU + HLSL.
answers.voice_tone: Technical and precise — favour accuracy over friendliness; assume the reader knows Go.
answers.design_principles: Correctness first, performance second; simplicity over abstraction; testability at every layer; no over-engineering beyond current phase requirements. TDD strictly enforced; separation of concerns across pipeline stages; right-handed coordinate system; column-major matrices.
answers.additional_standards: All phases follow trunk-based development with PRs; never commit directly to main; each phase must have task summary + docs updated before marking complete.
answers.language: Go 1.24, stdlib only for now; wgpu-native and GLFW bindings will be added in Phases 9–11.
answers.frontend: None — rendered output is a PNG file (MVP) or real-time window via GLFW (Phase 9+).
answers.backend: None — pure Go, no web server; the backend is the rendering pipeline itself.
answers.database: None — assets will eventually be loaded from OBJ files (Phase 16), but no database.
answers.infrastructure: Local development machine; CI runs on GitHub Actions (Linux, macOS, Windows matrix).
